verdict.rationale: Proa uses an islands model. Pages are server-rendered, and only components with signals or event handlers ship JavaScript. Each hydrated island gets its own small vanilla-JS module plus seed state on a shared runtime of about 1.3 KB gzipped, so the page hydrates piecemeal rather than as one whole-app bundle. Suspense boundaries also stream ready chunks out of order, so slow data does not block the page. Missing for 10: documented hydration scheduling or priority controls (e.g., on-visible or idle triggers), explicit 'progressive hydration' documentation, and independent time-to-interactive measurements.
